judgments.reasoning_cat1: The preamble mixes definitions with an odd shifting of duty — "Student and parent must determine the age of legal competency to sign contracts" — and the parenthetical "(under 18 years of age in most states)" leaves the minority threshold indeterminate; a scrivener's error ("thé") is present but harmless. The phrase "on Parent's behalf and on behalf of the minor student" is the sort of language courts do construe when asking whether a parent can bind a minor's claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with the operative release (c017), which likewise recites the parent signing "for myself and on behalf of the minor student," so there is no visible internal contradiction; the only tension is that this document assumes a parent can bind a minor while the severability clause (c023) contemplates parts being invalid. That is a legal-enforceability question rather than an internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This is essentially a recital describing activities and defining "inherent risks" as those "which cannot be eliminated without destroying the unique character of the activities" — a definitional standard that is vague at the edges and is expressly non-exhaustive ("among others," "some, but not all"). Because the release later turns on the inherent/non-inherent distinction, the definition could be argued over, though it tracks standard recreational-statute wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with c016, which says the description of inherent risks "is not complete," the two are consistent rather than conflicting; nothing in the operative release or indemnity contradicts this introduction. Its recital character against the broad operative assumption of ALL risks is a mild 2.3-type tension only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single descriptive sentence; "strenuous, physically and emotionally" is general but nothing turns on drawing its boundary. There is no operative obligation to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is one of the enumerated risk bullets feeding the assumption of risk in c016 and creates no conflict with any operative term. No other provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely descriptive of remoteness and delay in evacuation; "usually" and "may be significantly delayed" are hedges, not operative standards. Nothing here allocates a right or duty that two parties could read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably beside c019 (medical care and evacuation costs) and c016's assumption of risks. No contradiction located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words of pure description; "fail or malfunction" is plain and imposes no obligation. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the general assumption of risk in c016 and the release in c017; no provision anywhere warrants equipment condition, so no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive listing of camping and food risks; "offending food types" is loose but the sentence creates no entitlement. The list is illustrative and no catch-all bears legal weight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It intersects only loosely with the medical-disclosure duty in c018 (allergies described on the health form) and does not contradict it. No conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list closed by catch-alls — "other means," "other risks usually associated with such travel" — which could raise an ejusdem generis question if a travel mode were disputed, and the text is corrupted by an OCR/footer intrusion mid-sentence. Still, it is descriptive rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against c014 (NOLS not responsible for private contractors, "for example, transportation"), the two are complementary rather than conflicting. No inconsistency identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A descriptive catalogue of environmental hazards with "forces of nature" and "other mild or serious conditions" as open catch-alls; nothing operative depends on where those lines fall. Low intrinsic risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the inherent-risk framing of c002 and the assumption in c016 without contradiction. No other clause pulls against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This bullet acknowledges that instructor decisions are "imprecise and subject to errors in judgment," which is the disclaimer most closely tied to a negligence claim and could be read either as a mere risk description or as a substantive waiver of instructor negligence. That double reading is a genuine, nameable ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with c017, which releases negligence but expressly excludes gross negligence and intentionally wrongful conduct; a party could argue this bullet purports to assume all misjudgments, including grossly negligent ones, in tension with that carve-out. The tension is arguable but not squarely contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual statement; "most NOLS courses" and "at times" are hedged but nothing turns on their boundary within this sentence. No duty or right is allocated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears on supervision, which is also addressed in c011 (NOLS "cannot continually monitor") and in c018's admission discretion; those provisions point the same way. No conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scare-quoted term "free" time is itself undefined, and the clause distinguishes free time "before, during and after" the course while disclaiming responsibility only "before and after," leaving the during-course position ambiguous; the assertion that staff who accompany students act "as private individuals" is a further contestable characterisation. These are nameable ambiguities on which a supervision claim could turn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against c017, which releases "staff including employees, volunteers and interns" as Released Parties, so a staff member acting "as private individuals" is simultaneously inside and outside the released group; it also cuts against c018's statement that NOLS decides admission and removal in the student's best interests. That is a real, locatable friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive of foreign-program conditions; the final sentence, that field practices are "generally consistent with customs and standards used in the United States," reads as a qualified representation whose "generally" is vague. That sentence is the only part with any operative bite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the instrument warrants a standard of care, so the sentence is in mild tension with the blanket disclaimers of c016/c017 but not squarely contradicted. No conflicting provision identified.
